**Blues scale in the key of A**

| Note | Interval from previous note | Scale degree |
|------|-----------------------------|--------------|
| A    | —                           | 1 (root)     |
| C    | +3 semitones (minor 3rd)   | b3           |
| D    | +2 semitones (perfect 4th) | 4            |
| Eb   | +1 semitone (blue note)    | b5 (flattened 5th) |
| E    | +1 semitone (perfect 5th)  | 5            |
| G    | +3 semitones (minor 7th)   | b7           |

**Pattern of intervals (in semitones):**  
3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 3

So the A blues scale consists of the notes **A, C, D, Eb, E, G**. It’s essentially the A minor pentatonic (A, C, D, E, G) with an added “blue” note (Eb).
